speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a chronic cough and recurrent bouts of bronchitis; to determine the underlying cause, I need to ask you a few questions. Can you tell me exactly how long you have had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The 11-year duration of an aggressive cough with copious, thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis. Given the history of recurrent bronchitis requiring antibiotics, I need to confirm the structural airway damage. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT.
